name: Engines in thick air: sea-level loss sweep
description: An engine's nozzle opens onto the outside air, which presses back on the exhaust: at sea level it gives less thrust than in space. This sweeps how much less, from nothing to 30 %, for the same vacuum engine (SpaceX's Merlin 1D loses 9 %, the Space Shuttle's main engine 19 %). Up to 20 % the rocket still reaches orbit, losing around 100 m/s to back-pressure (Flight stats). At 25 % it lifts off too slowly and falls short; at 30 % the same tilt turns it over.
